brief: Media reports suggest NVIDIA's Board of Directors is preparing to replace Jensen Huang as CEO and is working with an outside firm on successor candidates. UBS argues the impact would be felt across three areas. First, financing: NVIDIA generates roughly $50-60B/quarter in free cash flow, a large portion of which recycles back into financing for neo-clouds, LLM developers, ecosystem partners and suppliers that Huang has personally driven; even a leader who maintains the same approach could pause these deals near term, potentially pulling $50B or more out of the system temporarily, at a time when rates are rising and parts of the credit market are less liquid. Second, supply chain: UBS views Huang as uniquely ahead of peers in locking in long-term agreements for memory, substrates and other inputs. Third, separately from the succession question, UBS flags risk of tighter US restrictions on shipments to China and to alternate regions such as Singapore, which was near 20% of revenue when NVIDIA last disclosed its geographic split; UBS estimates exposure at risk around 10% of revenue. UBS keeps its Buy rating and $300 price target unchanged, calling any succession impact a multi-year question.
